projects.name: Domain Scanner
projects.overview: A SaaS platform that audits domains and scores website security risks through automated SSL/TLS verification, open port discovery, DNS security validation, and HTTP security header compliance.
architecturalHighlights: Built asynchronous scanning pipelines with RabbitMQ (0.14ms dispatch latency), automated retry backoff, Redis caching, and PostgreSQL persistence with sub-second lookup times.
Implemented Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) separating administrative controls from standard tenant accounts.
Built tiered subscription tiers featuring daily usage caps, premium plans, request quotas, and Razorpay payment gateway integration.
Automated deployment pipelines on Oracle Cloud VM using Docker containers, GitHub Actions CI/CD, PM2 process management, and Nginx reverse proxy.

Security audit modules: SSL/TLS Encryption Check (TLS 1.3 protocol validation, CA chain checks, cipher strength), Port Scanner (non-blocking asynchronous scanning on ports 80, 443), DNS & Email Security (SPF record verification, DKIM checks, DMARC enforcement), and HTTP Security Headers (A+ rated header enforcement including CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, HSTS).

engineeringPhilosophy.description: From presales proof-of-concept and architecture alignment through Kubernetes deployment windows, reliable software requires owning the entire delivery pipeline, not just writing code.

engineeringPhilosophy.principle: 02. Throughput & Scale (Architecting for Real Request Volume)
engineeringPhilosophy.description: Designing high-volume decision engines (1,000–2,000 req/min) means treating latency and deterministic behavior as foundational constraints through deliberate database indexing and caching.
Long-running tasks belong in message queues with automated retries, DLQs, and cache persistence, keeping user-facing endpoints responsive and isolated from heavy downstream processing.
Modular architectures only succeed when teams uphold high standards for business-logic correctness, OWASP security practices, and active mentorship of new engineers.
